column1: # A committed record that a shared-config PACKAGE — as opposed to a tools/
# gate script — is genuinely consumed somewhere in the fleet, not merely
# published. check-clause-index.sh requires a row here before it will let a
# package-encoded clause claim `auto`; a package with no row here cannot,
# whatever the package itself contains. Standards' own dogfooding does not
# count as a row: a package describing its own consumer is not evidence
# anyone else acts on it, the same reasoning that keeps docs/ out of
# `consumers` is free text naming repo:mechanism pairs, comma-separated. This
# is not independently verified by the gate — it carries the same trust as
# any other committed claim in this repo, and is wrong exactly when someone
# commits something false, same as a wrong `Encoded by` path would be.
